name: tarp lean-to shelter: sloped tarp roof seen from above held by poles, open front with dark inside, bedroll and crate
label: wasteland_ruins/lean-to

answer.evidence: The tarp roof fills rows 1-17 as a large sloped plane with fold lines and seams. It ends in a light front-edge line at row 18, with a darker band at rows 15-17 above it and a dark row at 19 below it. Below that is a dark open front (rows 19-31) between the two poles, about 13 rows tall, with a bedroll and a crate inside. The roof is the top surface and the open front is the face, so it reads as three-quarter.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a tiny teal tarp roof with only about 3 lightness steps. It has a lighter top edge and a slightly darker lower band, and the rest is a smooth sheet with no per-tile scallops, grain or speckle. The measured near-flat coverage is 35%, against 0% for both references, so large areas are flat fills. The outline is a dark teal tone with no neutral black (0% near-neutral edge pixels), which is fine. The 10 visible tones per tile match the references' 10-12, but they come from a tiny object whose interior is mostly one flat colour. The dark inside, bedroll and crate are simple blocks with 1-2 tones and no texture. Beside the richly textured tile roofs, plaster and stone of the references, it looks flatter and more sticker-like, and I am not confident a careful artist would accept it.
